# synthcheck

**Experimental.** synthcheck checks how authentic synthetic survey
respondents are: Whether respondents generated by large language models
resemble the real people they are meant to stand in for.

It looks at three things:

- **Overlap:** Do synthetic respondents land where real people land?
- **Structure:** Do the items relate to each other as they do in real
  people?
- **Behaviour:** Do synthetic respondents answer the way people do,
  including variability, extreme and midpoint answers, acquiescence,
  consistency and person fit?

Each index is anchored between a shuffled baseline (0) and a second
sample of real people (100). The **synthetic authenticity benchmark**
compares several models in one table, scored by their weakest column by
default.

Three diagnostics sit beside the benchmark and do not change its score:
[`synthetic_construct()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthetic_construct.md)
checks whether the scales hold together and relate as they do in real
people (trait correlations, alpha and Tucker’s congruence against a
permutation null),
[`respondent_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/respondent_coverage.md)
checks whether every real person has a synthetic look-alike, and
`authenticity_benchmark(copula = TRUE)` adds a Gaussian copula row, a
generator without a language model, as a reference.

**No real data yet?**
[`synthetic_pretest()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthetic_pretest.md)
screens a new scale on synthetic respondents alone: Item-rest
correlations, items that barely vary or duplicate each other, reverse
keys, reliability, parallel analysis, IRT slopes, and whether the scales
you designed come back. It flags items in each model, temperature,
prompt wording or persona set and shows how many agree. This is pilot
screening, not validation: Language models answer more tidily than
people, so the pretest points to items to read again, and a field test
still decides.

Next to the pretest,
[`cognitive_interview()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/cognitive_interview.md)
runs simulated cognitive interviews: A language model plays each persona
you define, thinks aloud while it answers each item and answers standard
verbal probes, and a separate call codes the transcripts for
comprehension, retrieval, judgement, response-mapping and sensitivity
problems. It is a screening aid that points to wording to look at. It is
not a substitute for cognitive interviews with real people.

The package compares models and supports decisions about them. It does
not show that synthetic respondents can replace a field test.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("okanbulut/synthcheck")
```

## Example

``` r

library(synthcheck)

# Honesty-Humility, Canada: real people and six language models
h <- hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$trait == "H"]
rev_items <- intersect(h, hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$reverse])
keyed <- function(d) { d <- d[h]; d[rev_items] <- 8 - d[rev_items]; d }

real <- keyed(hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ])
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada" & hexaco_llm$attempt <= 4, ]
synthetic <- lapply(split(ca, ca$model, drop = TRUE),
                    function(m) lapply(split(m, m$attempt), keyed))

cov <- synthetic_coverage(synthetic, real, cor = "pearson")
cov
gg_coverage(cov)
```

The synthetic authenticity benchmark takes the raw answers and the item
table, and does the keying itself:

``` r

real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada", ]
synthetic <- lapply(split(ca, ca$model), function(m) split(m, m$attempt))

bm <- authenticity_benchmark(synthetic, real, hexaco_items)
bm
gg_benchmark(bm)

# the eight behaviour features behind the Behaviour column
gg_behaviour(bm$behaviour)

# with a Gaussian copula row as a reference
bm <- authenticity_benchmark(synthetic, real, hexaco_items, copula = TRUE)

# diagnostics
gg_construct(synthetic_construct(synthetic, real, hexaco_items))
gg_respondent_coverage(respondent_coverage(synthetic, real, hexaco_items))
```

## Generating synthetic data in an app

[`run_synthcheck_app()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/run_synthcheck_app.md)
opens an app that starts on an About tab with a guided tour and one
question: Do you already have real responses? With real data, the app
benchmarks the models; without it, the app pretests the scale on
synthetic respondents. Then it does the whole workflow: Define an
instrument and personas, generate synthetic respondents with Anthropic,
OpenAI or local Ollama models (with their temperature and the number of
attempts), watch a progress bar with the time left, save the data as
CSV, JSON, RDS or Excel, and benchmark the models against real data with
a plain-language summary for each one.

``` r

install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "ellmer", "callr", "jsonlite"))
res <- run_synthcheck_app(real = my_real_data)
res$benchmark
```

API keys typed into the app stay in memory for that session only. Keys
set as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.Renviron` are used
without being shown. The same steps work in code:

``` r

ins <- sc_instrument(hexaco_items[hexaco_items$trait == "H", ], scale = c(1, 7))
per <- sc_persona_grid(age = c(25, 45, 65), country = c("Canada", "the United States"),
                       template = "You are a {age}-year-old adult living in {country}.")
syn <- generate_synthetic(ins, list(sc_model("anthropic"), sc_model("openai")), per,
                          attempts = 5, respondents = 10, parallel = 8, output = "my_run")

real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
bm <- authenticity_benchmark(as_synthetic_list(syn), real, ins$items)
summarise_benchmark(bm)
```

See the [website](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/) for a Get
started article, tutorials on each step and a tour of the app with
demos.

## Data

`hexaco_real` holds 17,874 real respondents to the 240 IPIP-HEXACO items
from Canada, Great Britain and the United States (Open-Source
Psychometrics Project). `hexaco_llm` holds 89,597 synthetic respondents
from six language models (10 attempts per country), and `hexaco_items`
holds the item text, facets and keys.

## Citation

Run `citation("synthcheck")` for the citation, or use the “Cite this
repository” button on GitHub. Each release is archived on Zenodo
(<doi:%5B10.5281/zenodo.24173113>\](<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24173113>)).

## Related

synthcheck grew out of the coverage strip in
[mirtverse](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/). See the article
[Checking synthetic respondents: The coverage
strip](https://www.okanbulut.com/mirtverse/articles/synthetic-coverage.html).

# Package index

## Overlap and Structure

Where synthetic respondents land and how their items relate.

- [`synthetic_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthetic_coverage.md)
  : How well do synthetic respondents cover the real population?
- [`gg_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/gg_coverage.md)
  : Draw the coverage strip
- [`blend_llms()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/blend_llms.md)
  : Find the best blend of language models

## Behaviour

How synthetic respondents answer.

- [`synthetic_behaviour()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthetic_behaviour.md)
  : Behaviour: Do synthetic respondents answer the way real people do?
- [`gg_behaviour()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/gg_behaviour.md)
  : Draw the behaviour strip
- [`behaviour_features()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/behaviour_features.md)
  : The eight behaviour features of each respondent
- [`flag_careless()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/flag_careless.md)
  : Flag careless real respondents

## The synthetic authenticity benchmark

- [`authenticity_benchmark()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/authenticity_benchmark.md)
  : The synthetic authenticity benchmark
- [`gg_benchmark()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/gg_benchmark.md)
  : Draw the synthetic authenticity benchmark
- [`summarise_benchmark()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/summarise_benchmark.md)
  : Describe the benchmark in plain language

## Diagnostics

Checks beside the benchmark that do not change its score.

- [`synthetic_construct()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthetic_construct.md)
  : Construct structure of synthetic respondents
- [`gg_construct()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/gg_construct.md)
  : Draw the construct structure
- [`respondent_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/respondent_coverage.md)
  : Respondent coverage of synthetic respondents
- [`gg_respondent_coverage()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/gg_respondent_coverage.md)
  : Draw the respondent coverage
- [`synthetic_copula()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthetic_copula.md)
  : Respondents drawn from a Gaussian copula of the real data

## Pretest without real data

Pilot screening of a scale on synthetic respondents alone, with
agreement across conditions.

- [`synthetic_pretest()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthetic_pretest.md)
  : Pretest a scale on synthetic respondents, without real data
- [`gg_pretest()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/gg_pretest.md)
  : Draw the pretest
- [`summarise_pretest()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/summarise_pretest.md)
  : Describe the pretest in plain language

## Generating synthetic respondents

Define an instrument and personas, call language models, save the data.

- [`run_synthcheck_app()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/run_synthcheck_app.md)
  : Generate and benchmark synthetic data in a Shiny app
- [`sc_instrument()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/sc_instrument.md)
  : Define an instrument for synthetic respondents
- [`sc_personas()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/sc_personas.md)
  [`sc_persona_grid()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/sc_personas.md)
  : Define personas for synthetic respondents
- [`sc_model()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/sc_model.md)
  : Choose a language model for synthetic respondents
- [`sc_default_models`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/sc_default_models.md)
  : Default model ids
- [`sc_prompt()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/sc_prompt.md)
  : Build the prompts for one synthetic respondent
- [`generate_synthetic()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/generate_synthetic.md)
  : Generate synthetic respondents with language models
- [`write_synthetic()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/write_synthetic.md)
  [`read_synthetic()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/write_synthetic.md)
  : Save and read synthetic respondents
- [`as_synthetic_list()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/as_synthetic_list.md)
  : Turn a table of synthetic respondents into benchmark input

## Cognitive interviews

Screen item wording with language models playing personas, when there
are no real respondents yet.

- [`cognitive_interview()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/cognitive_interview.md)
  : Run cognitive interviews with language models playing personas
- [`sc_probes()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/sc_probes.md)
  : Probes for cognitive interviews
- [`sc_interview_prompts()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/sc_interview_prompts.md)
  : Show the prompts of a cognitive interview
- [`summarise_interviews()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/summarise_interviews.md)
  : Summarise cognitive interviews per item
- [`gg_interview()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/gg_interview.md)
  : Plot cognitive interview problems per item

## Data

- [`hexaco_real`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/hexaco_real.md)
  : HEXACO responses of real people, for checking synthetic respondents
- [`hexaco_llm`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/hexaco_llm.md)
  : HEXACO responses generated by six language models
- [`hexaco_items`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/hexaco_items.md)
  : The 240 IPIP-HEXACO items and their keys

## Helpers

- [`theme_synthcheck()`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/theme_synthcheck.md)
  : A clean ggplot2 theme for synthcheck graphics
- [`synthcheck`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthcheck-package.md)
  [`synthcheck-package`](https://www.okanbulut.com/synthcheck/reference/synthcheck-package.md)
  : synthcheck: Check how authentic synthetic survey respondents are
